hooks.text: Your Sunday plan doesn't fail on Sunday. It dies here.
Tuesday is when your motivation just... vanishes. Here's why.
You know exactly which day you'll quit. (Spoiler: it's not Monday.)
90% of students' plans don't make it past day three.
Your Sunday productivity system is already broken. You just don't know it yet.
That Sunday plan? Same one that failed last week.
You're not lazy. Tuesday just hits different.
Stop pretending Sunday's the day it all changes.
Plot twist: your biggest enemy isn't procrastination. It's Wednesday.
Imagine planning for the day you actually quit. Weird flex.

winner.text: Your Sunday plan doesn't fail on Sunday. It dies here.
winner.reasoning: Creates immediate intrigue (what day?) while naming the exact pain point this audience lives: making plans that collapse mid-week. The setup-payoff structure mirrors their own experience, making them *need* to swipe to see which day gets called out. Procrastinators recognize themselves instantly.

runner_up.text: You know exactly which day you'll quit. (Spoiler: it's not Monday.)
runner_up.reasoning: Slightly safer while maintaining curiosity and self-awareness humor. Works well if the winner feels too blunt for the feed's vibe, and the parenthetical adds personality without sacrificing clarity.

script.script:
[HOOK - 0-3 sec]
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: "Your Sunday plan doesn't fail on Sunday."]
Voiceover: It dies here.
[PAUSE]

[PROBLEM - 3-7 sec]
[CUT to you looking at phone]
Voiceover: You map out your whole week. Perfect schedule. But by Tuesday you're already off the rails.
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: "Why?"]
Because you planned like you're a robot.
[PAUSE]

[VALUE - 7-15 sec]
[CUT to writing/planning footage]
Voiceover: Here's what actually works: One anchor task per day. Not ten. One.
Then you time-block the rest backwards from there.
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: "1 anchor = actual progress"]
It sounds simple because it is. And that's why it sticks.
[PAUSE]

[CUT to direct address]
Voiceover: Stop planning like a perfectionist. Start planning like someone who actually finishes stuff.
[PAUSE]

[CTA - 15-17 sec]
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: "Follow for the full system"]
Voiceover: Follow for the full system that fixes this.
[CUT to call-to-action screen]
script.viewer_takeaway: One anchor task per day beats a perfect Sunday plan that falls apart by Tuesday. Following reveals the complete time-blocking system.

cover_options: Split screen: left side shows chaotic phone calendar with 10+ tasks, right side shows clean notepad with single task circled. Bold text overlay: 'Your Sunday plan dies here'
Close-up of hand crossing off one task on paper with satisfaction, blurred phone with overloaded calendar in background. Text: 'Stop planning like a robot'

frame_plan.on_screen_text: Your Sunday plan doesn't fail on Sunday.
frame_plan.visual_direction: First frame: direct camera look, casual setting (desk/couch). Slight head tilt. On-screen text appears in bold, modern sans-serif font. Background slightly out of focus.
Pause on face, serious but not dramatic expression. Deliver voiceover line with comedic timing.
Cut to POV shot: hand holding phone, scrolling through color-coded calendar app showing 8-10 tasks across the week. Multiple overlapping notifications visible.

frame_plan.on_screen_text: Because you planned like you're a robot.
frame_plan.visual_direction: Cut back to direct address. Shrug gesture. Slight eye roll or knowing smirk. Keep energy casual.
Cut to flat-lay desk shot: hand writing/circling ONE task on paper with pen. Minimalist aesthetic. Clean workspace. Text appears in striking color (contrasting with background).
Animation or b-roll of hand sketching time blocks on planner/calendar. Show visual hierarchy: one large box (anchor), then smaller blocks around it. Clean, organized motion.
Cut back to camera. Direct eye contact. Pointed gesture or hand motion for emphasis. Energy shifts to slightly more confident/instructional tone.

Cut to lower-third call-to-action screen with arrow pointing to 'Follow' button. Simple, clean design matching brand aesthetic. Hold for 2 seconds. Optional: quick flash of previous 'anchor' visual as background.

assets_needed: Phone with calendar app (multiple color-coded tasks visible)
Animation software (for time-block visualization) OR b-roll of hand-drawn calendar sections
On-screen text graphics (bold sans-serif, 2-3 accent colors max)
Optional: split-screen footage for before/after comparison shots

justifications.clarity: Hook + problem identified by 3 sec; 'one anchor task' concept lands clearly but takes until 7 sec to articulate the actual mechanism.
justifications.retention: Problem-to-solution arc keeps attention, but the 'time-block backwards' instruction needs visual reinforcement or viewers mentally check out at 10 sec.
justifications.save_potential: Core framework (anchor task + time-blocking) is actionable enough to save; viewers can implement immediately without the 'full system,' which weakens urgency.
justifications.shareability: Relatable hook, but lacks the 'wow' or laughable-honest moment that makes college students tag friends; feels educational rather than meme-adjacent.
justifications.audience_fit: Directly addresses procrastinator pain (Sunday plans failing by Tuesday); speaks to their failure pattern, not just productivity theory.
justifications.cta_strength: Clear ask (follow), but 'follow for the full system' implies gatekeeping content they already partially received, reducing friction incentive.

weaknesses.issue: The core value prop gets diluted: viewers learn the entire system (1 anchor + time-block) in the post, making 'follow for the full system' feel dishonest or redundant.
weaknesses.fix: Restructure CTA to highlight what *isn't* shown: 'Follow for: templates, the weekly audit that kills Sunday failure, + the exact hour-by-hour system.' Or front-load mystery: Cut the time-blocking explanation entirely and end at 'Here's the one thing that works—follow to see how to structure it.'

weaknesses.issue: Shareability is weak because the hook lands emotionally but the solution lacks a punchy, quotable moment; 'Stop planning like a perfectionist' is decent but not meme-ready for college audience.
weaknesses.fix: Replace '...like a perfectionist' line with something more self-aware and shareable: 'Stop planning like you're gonna become a different person Tuesday morning. You won't.' Or: 'Your Sunday self and Tuesday self aren't the same person. Plan for Tuesday self.'

weaknesses.issue: Time-blocking explanation at 10-13 sec is abstract without strong visual; hand-sketching or animation alone doesn't show *why* backwards time-blocking solves the robot-planning problem.
weaknesses.fix: Add voiceover logic during the time-block visual: 'You start with the task that actually matters. Then you build your day around protecting that time. Not the other way around.' Emphasize the decision hierarchy, not just the visual layout.

captions: Your Sunday plan doesn't fail on Sunday—it dies the moment you plan like you won't change by Tuesday. Here's the one rule that actually sticks: 1 anchor task. Everything else bends around it. Follow for the full system + the weekly audit that keeps you on track when motivation tanks.

Sunday plans hit different when you stop treating yourself like a robot. The anchor task method sounds simple because it is—but it's why people actually finish their week instead of rage-quit by Wednesday. Follow for the templates, the mistake-proof time-blocking setup, and the exact system that fixes this.
growth.final_call_reason: Strong hook and audience fit, but the CTA promise is undercut by delivering the core system in-video, and the shareability is dulled by a non-quotable solution moment—reframe the gatekeeping and punch up the behavioral insight to unlock higher engagement.
